name: Aalborg University
about: Aalborg University has about 17,700 students across three campuses — Aalborg, Esbjerg and Copenhagen — and is built entirely around problem-based learning, the 'Aalborg model'. Each semester splits into taught courses at the start and then a long group project, where four to six students work on a real problem, often one supplied by a company or public body, and are examined on the project as much as on the courses. You will spend a great deal of your degree in a project group room rather than a lecture hall. Only a handful of AAU's bachelor's degrees are taught in English, and most of them are engineering degrees in Esbjerg.
ibNotes: An IB Diploma with a minimum of 24 points meets AAU's general entry requirement.

IB Course Results (certificates rather than a full diploma) need at least 18 points, grade 3 or above in all six subjects, at least 3 subjects at Higher Level, and at least one subject at Danish A level and one at Danish B level.
AAU's IB results-service institution code is 000148 — give this to your IB coordinator so AAU can retrieve your results through IBIS.
The signature page from optagelse.dk must reach bacheloroptag@aau.dk by 15 March at 12:00 noon; without it the application is not processed.
AAU publishes a conversion chart showing which IB subjects and levels count as Danish A, B or C levels.
quotaNotes: All four English-taught bachelor's degrees have restricted admission. Quota 1 ranks applicants with convertible qualifications purely on the converted grade point average. Quota 2 holds 20 per cent of places and is decided on an overall assessment: the grades in the subjects that form the entry requirements, plus documented relevant activity of up to 12 months such as work experience or supplementary education. Applicants whose grades cannot be converted to the Danish scale are assessed only in quota 2. AAU publishes the previous year's quota figure on each programme page, and 'All Admitted' means everyone qualified was offered a place that year.

deadlines.label: Application (all international applicants, including IB)
deadlines.notes: AAU states: "Application deadline for all international students applying for a full bachelor's programme is 15 March, 12.00 noon (CET)."

deadlines.label: Signature page must reach AAU
deadlines.notes: Email the signed signature page from optagelse.dk to bacheloroptag@aau.dk. It must have arrived by the deadline.

deadlines.label: Application fee payment (non-EU/EEA)
deadlines.notes: EUR 150, paid through AAU's webshop; the receipt must be uploaded to optagelse.dk. Non-refundable once the application is submitted.

deadlines.label: Application status published
deadlines.notes: Check your result in unistart. Available study places also open on this date.

deadlines.label: Study start
deadlines.notes: All bachelor's programmes start on 1 September.

tuitionNonEu: Academic year 2026 (two semesters): DKK 115,700 for BSc Applied Industrial Electronics, BSc Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology and BSc Energy Engineering; DKK 55,600 for BSc Economics and Business Administration. Application fee EUR 150. EU/EEA students pay nothing.
notes: AAU lists exactly five bachelor's degrees for international students. Four are taught in English and are listed here. The fifth, Language and International Studies, English (Aalborg), is listed on the same page but its own programme page states the language of instruction is Danish and requires Danish A, so it is not included.
Three of the four English-taught degrees are at Campus Esbjerg on the west coast of Jutland, not in Aalborg. Esbjerg is a small port city and AAU's campus there is correspondingly small.

Problem-based learning is not a slogan at AAU: roughly half of each semester is a group project, assessed by an oral group examination. If you dislike sustained group work, this is worth knowing before you apply.

Applied Industrial Electronics admitted all qualified applicants in 2026, but AAU states that "From 2027, the programme is restricted in admission", which is the year an IB May 2027 cohort would enter.
AAU did not publish a quota figure for Energy Engineering on its programme page at the time of checking, although the page describes quota 1 and quota 2 selection.
Note AAU's own reminder that A, B and C are course levels, not grades; the minimum grade of 4.0 attached to Mathematics A is a grade on the Danish 7-point scale.
Application area number for Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology on optagelse.dk is 26525.

programmes.name: Applied Industrial Electronics
programmes.summary: You learn to build and control the electronics behind automated factories, robots and autonomous drones, mixing circuits, programming and control theory with semester-long projects. Later semesters split into two specialisations, Industrial Electronics and IT and Cyber Systems. Graduates go into process automation, wind energy and robotics.
programmes.requirementsText: Upper secondary school exam. English B. Mathematics A with a minimum average grade of 4.0. Physics B or Geoscience A.
extraRequirements: AAU states: "From 2027, the programme is restricted in admission. This means that you as an applicant are not sure of being offered a study place on the programme, even if you meet the admission requirements and apply on time."
Specialisations chosen during the programme: Industrial Electronics, IT and Cyber Systems.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology
programmes.summary: Chemistry and biotechnology taught together, with a lot of laboratory time in Esbjerg and a lot of computer modelling of chemical and biological processes. The projects lean towards the green transition, sustainability and pollution control. It is a small intake — 24 places in 2026 — so you will know everyone on your year.
programmes.requirementsText: Upper secondary school exam. English B. Mathematics A with a minimum grade of 4,0 in average. Physics B and Chemistry B, or Physics B and Biotechnology A, or Geoscience A and Chemistry B.
extraRequirements: Quota 2 holds 20 per cent of places and counts up to 12 months of documented relevant work experience or supplementary education.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Administration
programmes.summary: The standard Danish business economics degree — financing, economics, marketing, strategy and organisation — taught in English in Aalborg, with each semester built around a project done with or about a real company. It is the only one of AAU's English-taught bachelor's degrees that is not an engineering degree, and the only one based in Aalborg.
programmes.requirementsText: Upper secondary school exam. English B. Mathematics B. History B or History of Ideas B or Contemporary History B or Social Studies B or International Economics B.
extraRequirements: Quota 2 holds 20 per cent of places.

programmes.name: Energy Engineering
programmes.summary: Energy systems from both the thermal and the electrical side: wind turbines, solar cells, Power-to-X, biofuels and offshore installations, with laboratory work tied to problems from local industry. Two specialisations, Dynamic Systems and Thermal Processes, are chosen during the degree. Esbjerg is the centre of Denmark's offshore wind industry, which is why the programme sits there.
programmes.requirementsText: Upper secondary school exam. English B. Mathematics A with a minimum average grade of 4.0. Physics B and Chemistry C, or Physics B and Biotechnology A, or Geoscience A and Chemistry C.
extraRequirements: Quota 2 holds 20 per cent of places and counts documented relevant work experience or supplementary education of up to 12 months.
Specialisations chosen during the programme: Dynamic Systems, Thermal Processes.
